claims.claim: Amphilochius of Iconium was a fourth‑century Christian bishop who served as the bishop of Iconium in Lycaonia, having been born around 339/340 in Caesarea, Cappadocia and dying between 394 and 403.
He was a member of the Cappadocian theological circle, a first cousin of Gregory of Nazianzus and a close friend of Basil the Great.
In the sermon Amphilochius addresses a “heretic” who argues that the Father is greater because the Son is begotten, defending the co‑eternity and divine power of the Son.
Only a short fragment of the homily survives, making it one of the few extant pieces of Amphilochius’s theological writing; most of his works are lost.
